To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel scalable approach for approximate density-based clustering, that we implemented this approach in the open source framework ELKI, that we evaluated our approach on a large variety of datasets from various domains and that our approach outperformed the state-oftheart in all of our experiments.
We propose a new approach for scalable approximate DBSCAN based on locality sensitive hashing and representative point selection.

(1) we propose an efficient approximation of DBSCAN, ADvaNCE (Approximate Density-based Clustering Based on hashing and NEarest point selection), that is more scalable than existing approaches and (2) ADvaNCE is up to one order of magnitude more efficient than the most recent approximation approach for DBSCAN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
efficient clustering algorithms for massive data sets, where the number of data points is in the billions.
the development of scalable and efficient algorithms to analyse big data.
the following research questions: 1) How to approximate and accelerate DBSCAN?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is the fastest DBSCAN approximation technique in the state-of-the-art.
ADvaNCE is the fastest approximate DBSCAN approach to date.
ADvaNCE is an efficient and scalable approximation algorithm for DBSCAN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADvaNCE is an efficient and scalable clustering algorithm for massive datasets.
our approach is more accurate and scalable than the stateof-the-art.
we propose a new scalable and efficient clustering algorithm that can be used to analyse large amounts of data in a reasonable time.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of locality sensitive hashing and representative points selection can be used for speeding up DBSCAN in a scalable way, and that this approach is applicable to a wide variety of datasets and domains.
we can approximate DBSCAN with little precision loss and at a fraction of the time.
approximate density-based clustering can be made more efficient by reducing the overhead for computing distances.
